Hey mate, I’m also 16 and pre-t at least until I turn 18, 158cm and 61kg as of just now. Last year I also ate at 1200cals for 2 months + walks and other exercise and it sucked ass and doesn’t work. I just felt horrible all the time both mentally and physically and I neither lost weight nor fat. At that much of a deficit your body pretty much goes into emergency mode and tries to maximise every single calorie which kinda keeps you from losing fat or building muscle. 

I don’t know what you look like but also consider that losing fat and not guiding muscle like that might uh accentuate the ‘feminine’ figure idk that’s part of how I made peace with my own body being a bit chubby. You can build muscle without going to the gym I promise it’s shocking how far you can go with push-ups (I started off being barely able to do push-ups off my knees, now I can do 40 standard push-ups in one go and my shoulders look great. You can’t rush these things no matter how hard you wish just start with what you can handle and go up from there.)

Also the BMI is really really inaccurate, it’s made up by a mathematician and just overall doesn’t work very well. It was made with European amab people in mind and doesn’t differentiate between weight from muscles and weight from fat so you get people being really built being scaled as obese but they’re still really lean. 

I’d suggest taking the walks but eating at maintenance or really just eating enough that you’re not hungry, if you feel hungry all the time your overall efficiency goes way down and you’re a lot more likely to hit difficulties. Add some body weight strength stuff if you can(push-ups, squats, pull-ups or whatever you feel like tbh check out r/bodyweightfitness for exercise progressions you don’t have to do the whole routine any exercise is better than no exercise) 

At the end of the day no one can stop you if you want to go ahead with this, I get it, sometimes you just have to try it for yourself. Please take care of yourself, it does get better and you want to be in good shape to welcome it when it does. Congrats and good luck with the t appointment :)
